title: Bladder (urothelial) cancer
subtitle: Three diseases on one urothelium — NMIBC (TURBT + intravesical therapy; BCG is the backbone), MIBC (perioperative systemic therapy + cystectomy, or trimodality preservation), and metastatic (EV + pembrolizumab first line). Enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab now anchors both MIBC and metastatic disease
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, GU: Bladder Cancer (Khaki AR, Huober M) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Painless gross hematuria = bladder cancer until proven otherwise (smokers, aromatic amines, cyclophosphamide, pelvic RT, aristolochic acid, schistosomiasis → squamous). Microhematuria: risk-stratified cystoscopy ± imaging
Cystoscopy + TURBT with detrusor muscle in the specimen — without muscle, T2 cannot be excluded. Bimanual exam under anesthesia
Re-TURBT at 2–6 wk for any T1, incomplete resection, or no muscle in a high-grade specimen — up to half of T1 tumors are upstaged or have residual disease
CT urogram (or MR urogram / retrograde pyelogram if renal function is poor) — the upper tracts must be imaged: urothelium is a field defect. Urine cytology catches high-grade and CIS
MIBC: CT chest (or PET/CT), CBC, CMP. Bone scan / brain MRI only if symptomatic (brain MRI for small cell). Image before TURBT when possible — post-TURBT inflammation mimics T3/N+
Germline testing if young or Lynch-type family history — especially upper tract tumors (MSH2)

blocks.heading: Staging (AJCC 8th)
rows: Non-invasive papillary / carcinoma in situ (flat, high grade — the dangerous one)
Invades lamina propria — still NMIBC, but high-risk
Muscularis propria — a inner half, b outer half. The NMIBC / MIBC line
Perivesical fat (a micro, b macro) / a prostatic stroma, SV, uterus, vagina · b pelvic or abdominal wall
N1 single true-pelvis node · N2 multiple · N3 common iliac
II T2N0 · IIIA T3–4aN0 or N1 · IIIB N2–3 · IVA T4b or M1a (nodes beyond common iliac) · IVB M1b
blocks.footnote: ~75% present as NMIBC (Ta/Tis/T1) — recurrence is the rule, progression the risk. Grade (low vs high) matters in NMIBC; essentially all MIBC is high grade.

blocks.heading: Variant histology — changes management
rows: Aggressive, often understaged. Early cystectomy even for T1; BCG responses are poor
CDH1 loss; spreads along fascial planes and peritoneum — high positive-margin rate
Poor prognosis; treat as high-grade UC (NAC then cystectomy)
Treat like SCLC: neoadjuvant etoposide + platinum, then cystectomy or chemoRT. Brain MRI
Chemo-resistant — surgery-first. Urachal adeno (dome): partial cystectomy + umbilicus; colorectal-type regimens

boxes: TURBT (+ re-TURBT for T1) → risk group
intermediate: intravesical chemo or BCG ×1 yr
any cisplatin status (KN-905 vs RC; KN-B15 vs GC)
pT3–4 / N+ (no NAC) or ypT2+ / ypN+:
solitary, <5 cm, no hydro, no extensive CIS
EV not possible: cis-fit → nivo + GC, or
Later lines — test FGFR3 and HER2

blocks.heading: NMIBC risk groups (AUA)
rows: Low-grade Ta that is >3 cm, multifocal, or recurs <1 yr · high-grade Ta ≤3 cm · low-grade T1
High-grade T1 · any CIS · high-grade Ta >3 cm or multifocal · recurrent HG Ta · variant histology · LVI · HG prostatic urethra · BCG failure
blocks.footnote: EAU adds a very-high-risk tier (e.g. T1HG + CIS, multiple/large T1HG, variant histology, LVI) where immediate cystectomy is offered.

blocks.heading: NMIBC management
items: Single post-TURBT instillation (gemcitabine 2 g or mitomycin) within 24 h for suspected low/intermediate risk — SWOG S0337: recurrence HR 0.66. Skip if perforation or extensive resection
Low risk: surveillance cystoscopy (3 mo, then spaced out). Intermediate: intravesical chemo or BCG ×1 yr. High: BCG induction + maintenance ×3 yr
BCG: induction weekly ×6 (start 2–4 wk post-TURBT) → SWOG maintenance: weekly ×3 at months 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. Maintenance doubled median RFS (76.8 vs 35.7 mo)
BCG-naive high-risk: + durvalumab ×13 cycles (POTOMAC: DFS HR 0.68; FDA 28 May 2026) — grade 3–4 TRAEs 21% vs 4%
BCG shortage: reserve BCG for high risk; sequential gemcitabine + docetaxel is the workhorse alternative (phase 2: 3-yr HG-RFS 80%); randomized BRIDGE (vs BCG) pending

blocks.heading: BCG-unresponsive (FDA definition)
items: After adequate BCG (≥5/6 induction + ≥2 maintenance or second-induction doses): persistent/recurrent CIS within 12 mo, HG Ta/T1 recurrence within 6 mo, or T1HG at the first post-induction check
Radical cystectomy is the standard; bladder-sparing options (page 2) are for patients who decline or are unfit. Any muscle invasion → treat as MIBC

blocks.heading: Surveillance
items: NMIBC: cystoscopy + cytology q3–6 mo early, then annually (low-risk can space out faster); upper-tract imaging every 1–2 yr in high risk
Post-cystectomy: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis q3–6 mo ×2 yr, then annually; urethral wash if prostatic urethral involvement; B12 and renal function

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — the evidence: BCG-unresponsive NMIBC, MIBC perioperative and adjuvant therapy, bladder preservation, metastatic disease, upper tract

blocks.heading: BCG-unresponsive CIS — bladder-sparing (all single-arm)
rows: CR 82.4%, median DOR 25.8 mo; grade ≥3 TRAEs 13%. FDA 9 Sep 2025 (Inlexzo). Indwelling device, exchanged q3wk
CR 71% (FDA review 62%), median DOR 26.6 mo. FDA 22 Apr 2024 (Anktiva). Needs BCG supply
Adenoviral IFN-α2b gene therapy, q3 months: CR 53%, 46% of responders durable at 12 mo. FDA 16 Dec 2022
CR 41% at 3 mo, but few durable. FDA Jan 2020. Systemic irAE risk for a bladder-confined disease
Off-label, retrospective; cheap and widely used
blocks.footnote: Cretostimogene (oncolytic adenovirus, BOND-003: CR 75%, no grade ≥3 TRAEs) is not yet approved (BLA expected late 2026). Durable CR at 12 mo is the number that matters — roughly 20–45% across agents.

blocks.heading: Cisplatin eligibility (Galsky)
items: Ineligible if any: ECOG ≥2 · CrCl <60 mL/min · hearing loss grade ≥2 · neuropathy grade ≥2 · NYHA class III HF
CrCl 50–60: split-dose cisplatin (35 mg/m² d1 + d8) is common practice — measured 24-h CrCl can rescue borderline cases
Carboplatin does not replace cisplatin in the neoadjuvant setting — no survival benefit shown. In metastatic disease gem/carbo is acceptable

blocks.heading: MIBC — perioperative therapy
rows: Cis-eligible: perioperative EV + pembro vs neoadjuvant GC — 2-yr EFS 79.4% vs 66.2% (HR 0.53); OS HR 0.65; pCR 55.8% vs 32.5%. Grade ≥3 AEs 76% vs 67%. FDA 10 Jul 2026
Cis-ineligible or declined: EV + pembro vs cystectomy alone — 2-yr EFS 74.7% vs 39.4% (HR 0.40); OS HR 0.50; pCR 57.1% vs 8.6%. FDA 21 Nov 2025
GC + durvalumab → RC → durva ×8 vs GC → RC — 2-yr EFS 67.8% vs 59.8% (HR 0.68), OS HR 0.75. FDA 28 Mar 2025
ddMVAC ×6 vs GC ×4: neoadjuvant subgroup 5-yr OS 66% vs 57% (HR 0.71) — ddMVAC is the stronger chemo backbone, at the cost of more toxicity
Neoadjuvant MVAC: OS 77 vs 46 mo, pT0 38% vs 15%. Platinum combination NAC: 5% absolute 5-yr OS gain (HR 0.87)
blocks.footnote: No head-to-head of EV + pembro vs GC + durvalumab. EV+P now has OS data against both cystectomy alone and GC. Cystectomy = bladder, prostate/SV or uterus/anterior vagina, bilateral pelvic LND, and diversion (conduit or neobladder).

blocks.heading: Adjuvant after cystectomy
rows: Nivolumab ×1 yr vs placebo, ypT2+/ypN+ after NAC or pT3+/N+ without — DFS 20.8 vs 10.8 mo (HR 0.70). 5-yr: DFS HR 0.74, OS 75.0 vs 50.1 mo, HR 0.83 — not yet significant (follow-up ongoing). Benefit concentrated in PD-L1 ≥1%
Serial ctDNA ×1 yr; ctDNA+ → atezolizumab vs placebo: DFS 9.9 vs 4.8 mo (HR 0.64), OS 32.8 vs 21.1 mo (HR 0.59). Persistently ctDNA−: 2-yr DFS 88% untreated. FDA 15 May 2026 (Signatera CDx)
Pembrolizumab ×1 yr vs observation — DFS 29.6 vs 14.2 mo (HR 0.73); no OS gain shown

blocks.heading: Metastatic — first line
rows: vs platinum-gem, cis- and carbo-eligible alike: OS 31.5 vs 16.1 mo (HR 0.47), PFS 12.5 vs 6.3 mo (HR 0.45). Grade ≥3 TRAEs 56% vs 70%. The standard for everyone fit for it; no biomarker needed
Cis-eligible: OS 21.7 vs 18.9 mo (HR 0.78), PFS HR 0.72, CR 21.7% vs 11.8% with durable CRs. The option when EV is contraindicated (neuropathy, uncontrolled diabetes)
No progression after 4–6 cycles gem/cis or gem/carbo: avelumab maintenance — OS 21.4 vs 14.3 mo (HR 0.69). Start within 4–10 wk of the last cycle
blocks.footnote: Don't give chemo + pembrolizumab or chemo + atezolizumab (KEYNOTE-361, IMvigor130: no OS gain) — nivolumab is the only checkpoint inhibitor that adds OS to 1L platinum.

blocks.heading: Biomarkers & later lines
rows: Erdafitinib after ≥1 line incl. IO (THOR: OS 12.1 vs 7.8 mo vs chemo, HR 0.64). Full approval Jan 2024, FGFR3 only (FGFR2 dropped). Not instead of IO in IO-naive
T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg — tumor-agnostic accelerated approval (Apr 2024; DESTINY-PanTumor02 IHC 3+ ORR 61%). ILD 10.5%
Disitamab vedotin + toripalimab vs chemo: OS 31.5 vs 16.9 mo (HR 0.54). Approved in China, not US
Platinum doublet (gem/cis or gem/carbo); FGFR3 / HER2 agents; taxane; trial
EV monotherapy (EV-301: OS 12.9 vs 9.0 mo, HR 0.70). IO-naive after platinum: pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-045, OS 10.3 vs 7.4 mo)
Withdrawn for UC (Oct 2024) — TROPiCS-04 missed OS (HR 0.86) with 7% grade 5 AEs, mostly neutropenic infection

blocks.heading: Trimodality therapy (bladder preservation)
items: Maximal TURBT + concurrent chemoRT, then cystoscopic reassessment; salvage cystectomy for persistent/recurrent MIBC
Best candidates: solitary T2, <5 cm, visibly complete TURBT, no hydronephrosis, no extensive CIS, good bladder capacity
BC2001: RT + 5-FU/mitomycin vs RT alone — 2-yr locoregional DFS 67% vs 54% (HR 0.68); OS 48% vs 35% (NS). No randomized comparison with cystectomy
Lifelong cystoscopic surveillance — NMIBC recurrences in the preserved bladder are treated with TURBT ± BCG

blocks.heading: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma
items: ~5–10% of UC; renal pelvis > ureter. Lynch syndrome (MSH2) — screen with MMR IHC / germline testing; aristolochic acid (Balkan nephropathy)
Diagnosis: CT urogram + ureteroscopy with biopsy and cytology. Low-grade, small: kidney-sparing (endoscopic ablation, mitomycin gel)
High-risk: radical nephroureterectomy with bladder cuff. Consider neoadjuvant chemo — GFR falls after NU and may exclude cisplatin later
POUT: adjuvant gem + platinum (carboplatin if GFR <50) after NU for pT2–4/N+ — DFS HR 0.45; 5-yr OS 66% vs 57% (HR 0.68)
20–50% later develop bladder tumors — cystoscopic surveillance

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: 1 vial (50 mg) in 50 mL saline, dwell 2 h. Induction weekly ×6; maintenance weekly ×3 at mo 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36
Durvalumab 1500 mg IV q4wk ×13 + BCG induction + maintenance
Gemcitabine 2 g in 100 mL (dwell 1 h) or mitomycin 40 mg, <24 h
Gemcitabine 1 g, drain, then docetaxel 37.5 mg (2 h dwell) weekly ×6 → monthly maintenance
Gemcitabine 225 mg device, q3wk ×8 (6 mo) → q12wk ×6; removed after each 3-wk dwell
N-803 400 µg + BCG weekly ×6 (repeat once if no CR at 3 mo); maintenance ×3 wk at mo 4, 7, 10, 13, 19
MTX 30, vinblastine 3, doxorubicin 30, cisplatin 70 mg/m² d1 q14d + pegfilgrastim; ×3–6 neoadjuvant
Cisplatin 70 d1 + gemcitabine 1000 d1, 8 q21d (×4 neoadjuvant; ≤6 metastatic). Split: cis 35 d1 + d8
1500 mg d1 with GC ×4 → RC → 1500 mg q4wk ×8
EV 1.25 mg/kg (max 125 mg) d1, 8 + pembro 200 mg d1, q21d; pembro max 2 yr
Cis-eligible: ×4 neoadj → RC → EV ×5 + pembro ×13. Cis-ineligible: ×3 neoadj → RC → EV ×6 + pembro ×14
Nivolumab 360 mg + GC q3wk ×≤6 → nivolumab 480 mg q4wk, max 2 yr
Carboplatin AUC 4.5–5 d1 + gemcitabine 1000 d1, 8 q21d ×4–6
Nivolumab 240 q2wk / 480 q4wk ×1 yr · atezolizumab 1680 q4wk ×1 yr (ctDNA+)
8 mg PO daily; check phosphate at d14–21 → 9 mg if PO4 <9.0 mg/dL and no eye toxicity
5-FU 500 mg/m²/d fractions 1–5 + 16–20, mitomycin 12 mg/m² d1; RT 55 Gy/20 fx or 64 Gy/32 fx. Alt: weekly cisplatin 35–40 or twice-weekly gemcitabine 27 mg/m²

blocks.heading: Toxicity & monitoring
items: Enfortumab vedotin — boxed warning: SJS/TEN. Rash is common, usually in cycle 1: hold for grade 3 or suspected SJS/TEN, permanently stop if confirmed. Also peripheral neuropathy (cumulative, most common reason to stop), hyperglycemia/DKA (trials excluded HbA1c ≥8%), dry eye/keratitis, pneumonitis, extravasation
EV + pembro: rash can be EV or immune — a derm consult early saves the regimen. Dose-reduce EV (1.0 → 0.75 → 0.5 mg/kg) rather than dropping it

Erdafitinib: hyperphosphatemia is on-target (FGFR blocks FGF23 signaling) — low-phosphate diet, binders, dose adjust. Central serous retinopathy: ophthalmology exam monthly ×4 mo, then q3 months, and urgently for visual change. Also nail/hand-foot changes, stomatitis, dry eye

BCG: cystitis, fever <48 h is common. Do not instill with traumatic catheterization, gross hematuria, or active UTI (intravasation risk). BCG sepsis / BCGitis (persistent fever, pneumonitis, hepatitis, mycotic aneurysm): isoniazid + rifampin + ethambutol ± steroids — M. bovis is intrinsically pyrazinamide-resistant. Handle as a biohazard
Cisplatin: nephrotoxicity (pre/post hydration, Mg), ototoxicity, neuropathy; re-check eligibility every cycle. ddMVAC: neutropenia (G-CSF mandatory), mucositis, anthracycline cardiotoxicity
Checkpoint inhibitors: standard irAE surveillance — TSH, LFTs, cortisol; watch for pneumonitis and colitis. Intravesical agents (TAR-200, N-803) are mostly local urinary toxicity
After cystectomy: ileal conduit/neobladder → hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, B12 deficiency, stones, UTIs; neobladder needs a nocturnal voiding schedule

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: No muscle in the TURBT specimen = not staged
EV + pembro is now the answer in three settings: cis-ineligible MIBC, cis-eligible MIBC, and 1L metastatic
Nivolumab is the checkpoint inhibitor that works with platinum; pembro and atezo did not

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Perioperative EV + P vs GC, cis-eligible — OS HR 0.65
Perioperative EV + P vs RC alone — OS HR 0.50
Erdafitinib, FGFR3 after IO — OS HR 0.64
EV after platinum + IO — OS HR 0.70
BCG maintenance schedule — RFS 76.8 vs 35.7 mo
Adjuvant chemo for UTUC — DFS HR 0.45
